ai.description: This slender snake reaches 1 meter. It is light brown with a dark, zigzag vertebral stripe and a distinct "Y" or "V" mark on the head. It features a triangular head and large, cat-like pupils.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Boiga trigonata* is the distinct, dark-edged "Y" or "V" shaped marking on the top of its head, which sets it apart from other cat snakes.
ai.habitat: The Indian Gamma Snake inhabits dry, open landscapes, including scrub forests, rocky hills, and arid plains, typically ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Indian Gamma Snake is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting small lizards and rodents by prowling through low vegetation and rocky terrain under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Indian Gamma Snake is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–11 eggs. Breeding typically occurs between March and August, depending on the region.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian Gamma snake is widely distributed across the Indian subcontinent, ranging from arid plains and scrublands up to 1,500 meters in the Himalayan foothills.
